Descriptiontext

Lumilens is a private, venture-backed company founded in 2024 that designs and manufactures silicon photonics-based photonic interconnects for AI data center infrastructure, headquartered in San Jose, California, with operations in the United States and India/APAC. Its products are aimed at AI hyperscalers and large AI infrastructure operators that need to scale GPU clusters beyond the limits of copper and basic photonic transceivers, addressing bandwidth, thermal, and power constraints driven by exploding LLM and training cluster sizes. The company employs between 11 and 50 staff, including a leadership team drawn from Cisco, Juniper, Meta, Lumentum, and Coherent.

Lumilens' core product is a unified photonic interconnects platform that spans high-density pluggable, near-packaged, and co-packaged optics, positioned to support both scale-out (standards-aligned, cluster-to-cluster) and scale-up (ultra high-performance, direct GPU-to-GPU) architectures. The company claims its in-house silicon photonics and scale-up architecture can support 100x higher GPU-to-GPU direct connection density than existing solutions, enabling massive pod scaling and GPU disaggregation. Manufacturing is built around end-to-end automation with customized robotics and AI-optimized processes for die attach, wire bond, and active alignment, intended to deliver higher yield, product quality, supply chain continuity, and the ability to 'manufacture anywhere' through an open ecosystem.

The business model is B2B enterprise sales, with direct engagement of AI hyperscalers and infrastructure providers through a relationship-driven, technical-collaboration motion. Commercial vehicles include hardware product sales and joint development agreements; the most material disclosed commercial relationship is a May 2026 strategic joint development and supply agreement with POET Technologies, under which Lumilens placed a $50M initial purchase order for EOI-based optical engines targeting 800G and 1.6T pluggable transceivers, with a stated potential to scale to $500M+ in cumulative purchases over five years. The company has raised approximately $39M across two disclosed funding rounds (May 2024 $30M led by Mayfield; May 2025 $9.2M led by Accton Technology), is hiring into manufacturing, silicon photonics, and commercial functions, and is not yet generating commercial product revenue, with engineering samples expected late 2026 and hyperscaler production ramp targeted for 2027.
